conversations.title: Woman With Dwarfism Opens Up About Dating, and the Behavior She Can’t Ignore
conversations.reply: The creepy stuff she's naming is the real story here, not her dwarfism. Anyone treating a date like a spectacle instead of a person has already blown it before it started.

conversations.title: Parkinson’s drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone. - USA Today
conversations.reply: Doctors will happily talk through every other symptom of Parkinson's and go dead quiet the second sex comes up, and that silence is the real issue. Good that people are finally saying it out loud, because intimacy doesn't stop, it just stops getting talked about.

conversations.title: Time to Pay Attention: This Is Bigger Than Any One Policy - The NonProfit Times
conversations.reply: A quarter of adults living with a disability and still having to fight for protections that have existed for decades shows how shaky the ground still is. It's exactly why nobody can assume dating apps, or anywhere else, will just do right by disabled people without being pushed.

conversations.title: Aurora proclamation of Disability Pride Month seen as part of efforts to better support residents with disabilities - Chicago Tribune
conversations.reply: A proclamation costs nothing, the real test is what Aurora actually changes once July's over. A nice line at a council meeting means little if the buses and buildings look exactly the same come August.

conversations.title: How a San Diego woman's autism diagnosis led to a journey of self-discovery - NBC 7 San Diego
conversations.reply: Getting that answer at 42 and finally making sense of herself is huge, and she's right that it doesn't define her. Disclosure, whether it's a diagnosis or a first date, should be met with curiosity, not someone quietly disappearing.

conversations.title: Leeds Pride 2026 Set to Draw 60,000 as City Marks 20 Years of Celebration - Public Sector Executive
conversations.reply: 60,000 people in Leeds city centre is brilliant, but the real test is whether every one of them can actually get through the crowd and onto the dancefloor. A step-free route to the party matters just as much as the party itself.

conversations.title: Performers at Burton Street Foundation show off their talents - BBC
conversations.reply: A drag show and a full festival built around performers with learning disabilities taking centre stage is exactly what a night out should look like more often. Sheffield's set the standard here, other venues just need to catch up.

conversations.title: Co-op extends festival sponsorship deal with Live Nation until 2031 - Retail Gazette
conversations.reply: Five more years of pop-up shops is an easy headline, a sponsorship deal that never once mentions access at the festivals it's tied to is missing the actual point. Show us the accessible viewing platforms and the step-free routes, that's the extension worth talking about.

target_reply: Shani, the fight you've spent years pushing on visibility is the exact same fight happening in dating, it just hasn't had its moment yet. Able2Love would love you to see what's being built, feels like exactly the kind of noise you'd want in your corner.
funding: Nothing new today, worth knowing about: UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk), Stelios Awards (around March)
moment: July is Disability Pride Month, and with Leeds Pride pulling in 60,000 people this weekend, the funniest way to join in is asking where the accessible entrance is before you ask where the bar is.
target: Shani Dhanda (UK disability activist and broadcaster)

x_candidates.author: legaltweetz
x_candidates.post: I was single for many years. I casually dated here and there ... I casually dated here and there. But nothing serious for over a decade. It wasn't alcohol for me but endometriosis and disability. I think you're smart for
x_candidates.reply: A decade of nothing serious isn't a reflection on you, it's what happens when the world makes dating so much harder for endometriosis and disability than it ever needed to be. Good on you for still putting yourself out there.

x_candidates.author: serenebutterfly
x_candidates.post: "As my disability became more visible, I began laying extra ... "As my disability became more visible, I began laying extra claim to certain parts of my identity as a woman as if I somehow needed to counterbalance. When I
x_candidates.reply: That urge to counterbalance says so much about how the world reacts to visible disability, not about how much of a woman you are. You were never lacking anything to prove.

x_candidates.author: ritagayworths
x_candidates.post: it's so hard being disabled/chronically ill when you're single ... it's so hard being disabled/chronically ill when you're single and live alone.....i value my independence and having my own space so much but i can't manage
x_candidates.reply: Wanting your own space and struggling with doing everything solo aren't contradictions, they're just both true at once. That's a hard balance and you're allowed to feel it.

x_candidates.author: Favwontmiss
x_candidates.post: Dating a neurodivergent person means understanding that ... Dating a neurodivergent person means understanding that emotional safety matters. You can't constantly create confusion, break trust, and then expect their
x_candidates.reply: Exactly this, emotional safety isn't a bonus feature, it's the whole foundation. If someone can't hold that steady they're not actually ready for the rest of it.

x_candidates.author: Favwontmiss
x_candidates.post: Dating while neurodivergent means you're not just asking “ ... Dating while neurodivergent means you're not just asking “do I like this person.” You're asking “can I be dysregulated around this person and still feel safe.
x_candidates.reply: That second question is the real one most people never even think to ask. Feeling safe enough to be dysregulated around someone tells you everything about whether it works.
